title: Molecular Etiology and Mortality Risk Stratification of Non-SARS-CoV-2 Severe Acute Respiratory Infection in a Predominantly Pediatric Cohort: A Retrospective Study From a Tertiary Care Hospital in North India - Cureus

analysis.time: The study was conducted between September and December 2021, with data analysis undertaken in the post-pandemic phase (2022 onwards).
analysis.location_and_population: A tertiary care hospital in North India, with a predominantly pediatric population of 103 children and 14 adults.
analysis.event: A retrospective study evaluated the etiology of non-SARS-CoV-2 severe acute respiratory infections (SARI) and the prognostic utility of the ViVI Disease Severity Score (ViVI Score) in hospitalized patients.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The study included 117 patients, with an overall mortality rate of 20.5%. Among patients with culture-confirmed sepsis, mortality increased to 60%. The ViVI Score showed excellent mortality prediction (AUC 0.946) with a cutoff of ≥30 yielding 83.3% sensitivity and 91.4% specificity.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The study used multiplex PCR and conventional microbiological culture for pathogen identification. It also measured serum C-reactive protein (CRP), procalcitonin (PCT), and D-dimer. The findings suggest the need for improved diagnostic methods and clinical risk stratification in resource-constrained settings.

analysis.brief_en: This retrospective study from a tertiary care hospital in North India analyzed non-SARS-CoV-2 severe acute respiratory infections (SARI) in 117 hospitalized patients, including 103 children and 14 adults, admitted between September and December 2021. The study aimed to evaluate the etiology of SARI and the prognostic value of the ViVI Disease Severity Score (ViVI Score) in a predominantly pediatric cohort. Using multiplex PCR and conventional microbiological culture, respiratory pathogens were identified, with human respiratory syncytial virus (HRSV) A/B being predominant. Blood cultures were positive in 34.2% of patients, mostly yielding methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus. Overall mortality was 20.5%, rising to 60% among patients with culture-confirmed sepsis. The ViVI Score demonstrated excellent mortality prediction (AUC 0.946) with a cutoff of ≥30 showing 83.3% sensitivity and 91.4% specificity. The study highlights the importance of accurate pathogen identification and early risk stratification to improve patient outcomes and reduce unnecessary antibiotic use, especially in resource-limited settings like India. The findings suggest that integrating rapid molecular diagnostics with standardized severity assessment tools could enhance clinical decision-making and respiratory disease surveillance.
